what: Time from opening a conversation to the PAINTED frame that carries its first feed rows, on a production build, before and after the persisted tail cache.
driver: bun scripts/profile-reopen.ts --cdp-port 0 --runtime <the pinned bun> --repeat 3 --json <file>, once against a build of main (before) and once against a build of this branch (after), back to back on the same machine
runtime: the Bun pinned in the Dockerfile, serving `next start` (never `next dev`)
browser: headless Chrome over raw CDP, foregrounded, with background throttling disabled
milestone: the first frame showing rows of the target a reader can see - laid out, not hidden by CSS anywhere up their chain, not inert, with part of their box left once the viewport and every clipping ancestor (the transcript scroller included) have cut it - in the pane that is active for it (the focused pane on the phone, the target's board pane on the desktop). `rows` counts only those rows, so it is what the scroller shows and not what the window holds. The DOM check must still hold in both animation frames that follow; a milestone no frame confirms within a second is rejected and the run fails, so `rafConfirmed` is true in every sample kept here.

attribution.storedTails: conversations with a persisted tail in the store as the document's first script read it. A hint only: Chrome hands a new renderer its own snapshot of the origin's storage, so a tail written by the previous document can be missing from it and still be restored by the app. Which path painted is read off the paint: rows on screen before any transcript bytes arrived came from the cached tail (firstBytesMs null), and a cold sample that did so is retaken.
attribution.firstBytesMs: when transcript bytes for this conversation first reached the page BEFORE the paint: a stream chunk carrying this conversation's subscriber id, or a POST /api/logs poll whose own request named this conversation, stamped when its body COMPLETED and only when the answer held bytes for it (`via`). Null means the rows were painted without waiting for any.
attribution.revalidatedMs: when those bytes arrived at all, before or after the paint.
attribution.parseRenderMs: bytes in hand → the painted frame: the client's own parse and render, with `blockingMs` the main-thread long-task time inside it.
attribution.payloadKb: size of that first delivered chunk as it came over the wire.
attribution.note: A resource entry's responseEnd cannot report this: the Viewer's log stream never ends, so its entry closes only when the page does.

statistic: median of 3, with the min-max spread and the per-sample attribution in the strings; the raw samples are below each case.
